summary: Asheville on Bikes is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit bicycle/multimodal advocacy organization with a board, staff and coaches, hundreds of dues-paying and volunteer members, and an ongoing after-school cycling program. The four assigned units (Pumpkin Pedaller, Ride of Silence, Spring Out, Strive Not to Drive Week) are open public rides and a campaign week run by the org for the general public, but the org itself is a persistent membership-based advocacy group distinct from any single event.

evidence.note: Site describes the org as a nonprofit with a board of directors and dedicated staff/coaches page, run under a formal structure rather than an ad hoc event host.
Page describes volunteers as 'the lifeblood of our day-to-day operations' plus after-school cycling programs and donations, indicating an ongoing volunteer base rather than a rotating public.
Confirms Asheville on Bikes Incorporated is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit (also listed on ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer).
Org runs a dedicated 'AoB Membership Night' event, and search results describe 'hundreds of members who speak with one voice' on advocacy issues.
Ride of Silence listing frames the ride as community remembrance/advocacy for cyclist safety, consistent with an advocacy org's public programming rather than a commercial event.

Spring Out and Strive Not to Drive Week listings both explicitly cite 'advocacy' and 'bike advocacy' as part of the ride/campaign purpose, tying the events back to the parent org's mission rather than a one-off host.
